caption:
🌸 Summer DIY 🌸 Flower Arrangement

Our collaborator @simplystyledinspo shares a creative way to transform a vintage glass shade and lace doily into a beautiful summer flower arrangement! 💐

With just a few simple Thrift Store finds, you can create a charming centerpiece that feels vintage, unique, and full of summer charm. 🌿

Steps:

1. Find a vintage glass shade
2. Find a lace doily
3. Place the lace doily over a glass shade or vase and secure it with a rubber band
4. Create your DIY flower frog
5. Place the shade over the flower frog
6. Add your favorite summer blooms
7. Arrange, display, and enjoy!

A little creativity can give thrifted treasures a whole new life and is a whole lot of fun ✨ 

Plus, your DIY flower arrangement with finds from The Salvation Army Thrift Store supports local programs and services like food banks and shelters, and helps the planet breathe easier through re-use 💙

Easy Tiramisu (no eggs) recipe:

Ingredients:
• 1 1/2 cups heavy whipping cream
• 8 oz mascarpone cheese, room temperature
• 1/3 cup granulated sugar
• 1 tsp vanilla extract
• 1 1/2 cups cold espresso
• 3 tbsp coffee liqueur (optional)
• 1 package lady fingers
• Cocoa powder, for dusting

Instructions:
In a bowl, whip the heavy cream until soft peaks form. Add sugar + vanilla and continue whipping until stiff peaks form. Gently fold in mascarpone until smooth and combined.
In a shallow bowl, combine espresso + coffee liqueur. Quickly dip each lady finger into the coffee mixture (don’t soak them).
Layer dipped lady fingers into the bottom of dish. Spread some of the mascarpone mixture over top. Repeat with another layer of dipped lady fingers and continue with remaining mascarpone cream and lady fingers.
Dust generously with cocoa powder. 
Refrigerate for at least 3–4 hours, preferably overnight.
Serve chilled and enjoy!

caption:
No matter where you’re from, eggs have a way of connecting cultures, kitchens, and stories - passed from one generation to the next.
I made Bacalhau à Gomes de Sá as it is deeply rooted in my Portuguese heritage. A recipe built slowly and intentionally, layering salted cod, tender potatoes, onions, olives, and generous olive oil, then finished with sliced boiled eggs and fresh parsley.
The eggs are essential, bringing balance, richness, and that final comforting touch. I used @farmersfinesteggs sourced from local Alberta farmers. This is such a special dish in our family, it carries flavours that hold memories: evoking the smells, warmth, and memories, shared across generations. Recipe below.

#recipeideas #recipeshare #dinnerinspo #dinneridea #easydinners 

Bacalhau à Gomes de Sá

Ingredients:
3–4 frozen cod fish fillets, thawed
1½ lbs Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled
1 large onion, thinly sliced
2 cloves garlic, minced
½ - ¾ cup good-quality olive oil, plus more to finish
3–4 hard-boiled eggs, sliced
½ cup pitted black olives, sliced
1-2 bay leaves, optional
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
Fresh cracked black pepper

Instructions:
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Prepare the Cod
Thaw the cod completely, then gently simmer in salted water, along with the bay leaves, for 6–8 minutes until just cooked.
Drain, remove any bones and skin, flake into large pieces. Discard the bay leaves. Set the cod aside. 
Cook the Potatoes
Boil potatoes until just fork-tender. Slice into rounds. Set aside. 
Sauté the Base
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add onions and cook slowly until soft and lightly golden. Stir in garlic and cook until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper. Add in cod fish, followed by the sliced potatoes and chopped parsley. Toss together very gently and remove from heat.
Layer the Dish
Liberally grease a large casserole dish with olive oil. Add the cod and potato mixture altogether to the dish. Place in preheated oven and bake for 25-30 minutes until golden and warmed through. 
Finish with Eggs
Remove dish from oven and top with sliced hard-boiled eggs and olives. Drizzle with additional olive oil and garnish with chopped parsley.

Ingredients:
1 milk chocolate bar
1 dark chocolate bar
1 white chocolate bar
1 cup mini chocolate eggs, chopped
Instructions:
Preheat & prep:
Preheat oven to 250°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Melt chocolate:
Place all three chocolate bars on the prepared baking sheet. Pop in the oven for 5–8 minutes, checking every 2 minutes, until soft but not burnt.
Swirl together:

Add mini eggs:
Sprinkle the chopped mini eggs evenly over the melted chocolate. Press lightly so they stick.
Chill:
Transfer the baking sheet to the fridge for 20–30 minutes, until fully set.
Break & serve:
Remove from fridge and break the chocolate into shards. Enjoy!

Strawberry Cream Cheese Pastry Heart

Ingredients:
2 cans crescent roll dough
100g cream cheese, softened
⅓ cup strawberry jam (thick-style)
Zest of ½ lemon

Almond Glaze:
⅓ cup icing sugar
¼ tsp almond extract
2–3 tsp cream

Instructions:
1. Prep
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Assemble the Heart
Unroll crescent dough and separate into triangles.
Arrange triangles in a large heart shape on the baking sheet:
Points facing outward
Wide ends slightly overlapping in the centre
Spread cream cheese over the overlapping dough.
Sprinkle lemon zest evenly over the cream cheese.
Spoon strawberry jam over the cream cheese (don’t over fill).
Fold the pointed ends of the dough over the filling toward the centre, pressing gently to secure and shape heart.
3. Bake
Brush top of dough with egg wash.
Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes, until golden and puffed.
Let cool slightly.
4. Make the Icing
Whisk icing sugar and almond extract.
Add cream 1 tsp at a time until thick but drizzleable.
5. Finish
Drizzle icing over the pastry.
Optional: dust lightly with extra icing sugar.

Chocolate molten lava cake

Ingredients:
1 cup dark chocolate, broken into small pieces 
½ cup unsalted butter

2 whole eggs

½ cup all-purpose flour
Pinch of salt

Stir until glossy and smooth
Let cool slightly
3. Whisk Eggs + Sugar
In a bowl, whisk:
Eggs
Egg yolks
Sugar
Mix until slightly thick
4. Combine
Slowly pour chocolate mixture into eggs
Add vanilla
Fold in flour and salt until just combined
(Don’t overmix)
5. Fill Cocotte
Pour batter into prepared cocotte
Fill about ¾ full

425°F

Roasted Cosmic Crisp® Apple Cider Honeycrisp Soup

	•	4 Cosmic Crisp® apples, peeled, cored, chopped
	•	1 small onion, sliced

	•	1 tbsp butter
	•	1 tbsp olive oil

Because Christmas mornings deserve these gingerbread pancakes and the @ourplace pan makes them perfect every time! What are your holiday breakfast traditions? 🌲🥞 

Gingerbread Pancakes 

Ingredients
For the pancakes:
* 1 cup all-purpose flour
* 4 tbsp brown sugar
* 1 tsp baking powder
* 1/2 tsp baking soda
* 1/2 tsp salt
* 1½ tsp ground ginger
* 1 tsp ground cinnamon
* 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
* 1/2 cup sour cream
* 1/2 – 2/3 cup milk (adjust for desired batter consistency)
* 1 large egg
* 2 tbsp melted butter
* 1 tsp vanilla extract
For topping:
* Whipped cream
* Fresh cranberries (or sugared cranberries)
* Maple syrup
* Powdered sugar for dusting

Directions
1. Mix dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, ginger, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
2. Mix wet ingredients: In another bowl, whisk together sour cream, milk (start with 1/2 cup, add more if needed), egg, melted butter, and vanilla until smooth.
3. Combine: Pour wet ingredients into dry and stir until just combined. Small lumps are okay, don’t overmix. Add extra milk if batter feels too thick; it should be pourable but still thick enough to hold its shape.
4. Heat your pan: Preheat a non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium heat. Brush lightly with butter for shine.
5. Cook pancakes: Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook another 1–2 minutes until golden brown.
6. Serve: Stack pancakes, top with whipped cream, cranberries, drizzle with maple syrup, and dust lightly with powdered sugar.

Edward “Ted” Troughton, Managing Director of The Salvation Army’s National Recycling Operations, which oversees all Salvation Army thrift stores across Canada, earned $304,739.84 in 2024, according to Ontario’s official Sunshine List. Since 2018, Troughton’s salary has increased by 71%, rising from approximately $178,508 to over $304,000. And for what?

Wages that, in most cities, fall far below the cost of living.

 

Meanwhile, the executive tier enjoys:

Six-figure compensation

Above average regular salary increases.

This is not just a pay gap.

It is a values gap.

 

The Salvation Army promotes its thrift stores as social enterprises that generate funding for essential community programs. But when the workers who enable that mission are underpaid and overstretched, the model begins to look less like charity, and more like exploitation.

 

It’s time to ask tough questions:

 

Why is executive compensation growing rapidly while retail staff struggle to survive?

 

How can a charitable organization justify this level of inequity within its own workforce?

 

Charity must begin at home.

And that means paying your own people fairly! @uniforcanada

What does it say when a charity pays its top executive over $300,000, while the people running its stores can barely afford groceries or rent?

 

Edward “Ted” Troughton, Managing Director of The Salvation Army’s National Recycling Operations, which oversees all Salvation Army thrift stores across Canada, earned $304,739.84 in 2024, according to Ontario’s official Sunshine List. That’s almost $100,000 more than the premier of Ontario makes!

 

But the story doesn't end there.

 

Since 2018, Troughton’s salary has increased by 71%, rising from approximately $178,508 to over $304,000. That’s a jump of nearly $126,000 in just a few years, during the same period that many front-line employees saw little increase in their pay, aside from modest, government-mandated minimum wage adjustments.

 

And for what?

Wages that, in most cities, fall far below the cost of living.

 

Meanwhile, the executive tier enjoys:

Six-figure compensation

Above average regular salary increases.

This is not just a pay gap.

It is a values gap.

 

The Salvation Army promotes its thrift stores as social enterprises that generate funding for essential community programs. But when the workers who enable that mission are underpaid and overstretched, the model begins to look less like charity, and more like exploitation.

 

It’s time to ask tough questions:

 

Why is executive compensation growing rapidly while retail staff struggle to survive?

 

How can a charitable organization justify this level of inequity within its own workforce?

 

Charity must begin at home.

And that means paying your own people fairly!

caption:
Luscious 3 ingredient mousse served in thrifted tea cups, perfect for Easter and spring/summer entertaining!

3 Ingredient Chocolate Mousse

Ingredients
* 1 cup (6 oz) Good Quality Semi-Sweet Chocolate Chips
* 1 ½ cups Heavy Whipping Cream (divided: 1/2 cup for melting, 1 cup for whipping)
* 1-2 Tablespoons Powdered Sugar
* Optional: 1/2 tsp vanilla extract or a pinch of salt to boost flavor 

Instructions
1. In a medium microwave-safe bowl, combine the chocolate chips and 1/2 cup of heavy cream. Microwave in 20-second increments, stirring well in between, until the chocolate is melted and smooth. Set aside to cool to room temperature. Do not let it become completely solid again.
2. In a separate chilled bowl, whip the remaining 1 cup of heavy cream (and powdered sugar/vanilla if using) with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.
3. Gently fold one-third of the whipped cream into the cooled chocolate mixture. Then, gently fold in the remaining whipped cream until just combined, don’t over-mix.
4. Spoon the mousse into teacups. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to allow it to set into a firm texture.
